gaps.sentence: 'Watch out for the ice on the road,' she said. She ___ us about the icy road.
gaps.explanation: Warnings about a danger: warn somebody about something (or warn sb to do).

gaps.sentence: "It was your fault." — They blamed me ___ the accident.
'OK, I'll help you move house,' she said. She ___ to help me move house.
gaps.explanation: Agreement to a request is reported as agreed to do something.

gaps.sentence: "I will call you tomorrow." — She said she ___ me the next day.
'I really must have that report by five,' the editor said. The editor ___ on having the report by five.
gaps.explanation: Insisting on a demand: insist on + -ing (or insist that + clause).

gaps.sentence: 'I'll be waiting outside the cinema,' he said. He said he ___ waiting outside the cinema.
gaps.explanation: will be + -ing becomes would be + -ing in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I might take a gap year,' he said. He said he ___ take a gap year.
gaps.explanation: Might has no further backshift form; it stays might.

gaps.sentence: 'Could you open the window?' she asked. She asked me ___ the window.
gaps.explanation: 'Could you...?' requests are reported with ask + object + to-infinitive; no could remains.
